title: How George got his flute and clarinet
summary: She refused him a clarinet, but he bought a dime flute and later his father bought a second-hand clarinet on Canal Street.

blocks.x: rag dolls for all of us. I was wondering a little bit about the George's early life we didn't get to talk so much to George the other time. No. When he first took up his clarinet and started playing you mentioned you taught him one little song was that on his little flute or on his clarinet? No on the flute. On the flute. How long did he play that

flute before he took his clarinet? He wanted the clarinet you know and George was always small and I thought George wouldn't live to see 15 years I didn't want to give. I said I'll give you a violin but I'll not give you a clarinet because you'll die before you're 15 years old. And he oh no more I don't want no violin I want a clarinet. Well I never did give it to him until one day he asked I sent him to bring because I used to wash plenty shirts and more so. I sent him to bring a basket of clothes by Mr. Grima on St. Louis Street. I had sent him around the corner to bring some clothes and I gave him a nickel I believe a nickel or a dime I don't remember. When he come back I said well now go bring Mr. Edgar Grima's clothes or shirts and collars. They wore collars the tash. Oh yes I did too. Yeah. And he said Mo can I get can I get a flute? I said no thank you George I just gave you I don't remember it was a nickel or a dime. He said it only cost a dime. I said go ahead and get it. And he went and he got that little ten cents flute and that's where he started. Tululu, And I never never give him a clarinet. And one day he went with his father on Canal Street and was looking in the showcase and he told his papa you see I want that and mama don't want to give it to me. And his father said well let's go and get and see. So he went inside and Mr. the clerk told him it's for this little fella. He told him yes. He said well I he's a beginner I have a small one second hand I suppose but it's forty dollars. For a beginner it's all right. And that's where he went he started that's where he started with the clarinet. But I never give him no clarinet.
